extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and authors preparing or submitting manuscripts to the Journal of the American Mathematical Society (JAMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting research articles to the Journal of the American Mathematical Society, including peer-review process, submission mechanics, required metadata, and post-acceptance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles appearing in this journal are peer reviewed by external reviewers. Journal of the AMS has a single-anonymous peer-review process in which the reviewers know who the authors of the manuscript are, but the authors do not have access to the information on who the peer reviewers are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style. Questions about the initial submission process should be directed to [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre-review rejection grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit ground for desk rejection (no external review) and includes both topical unsuitability and clear scientific/presentation weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS uses Centralized Manuscript Processing for initial submissions. The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An alternate method is to send one copy of the paper to Centralized Manuscript Processing (postal address provided). If sending a paper copy, required identifying/contact information must be included to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information for mailed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper copy is being forwarded to the AMS, the following information is required with the submission (note that all contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay): Name of the journal to which the paper is submitted; Name of the corresponding author; Contact information including email address and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing complete contact information is necessary to avoid processing delays when using the alternate postal submission route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to indicate which editor they consider appropriate for their manuscript as part of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on simultaneous submissions or submissions of previously published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must supply primary and secondary MSC codes (2020) as part of the manuscript metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although an abstract is not required upon initial submission, upon acceptance authors will be requested to supply an abstract for the electronic version of this journal. An abstract should be at least one complete sentence and at most 300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS offers free worldwide access to the electronic abstracts. No abstracts appear in the printed journal starting in 1998.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected. After acceptance, authors should follow the online Submission Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged use of AMS style files and author resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX Resources, the AMS Style Guide, the Mathematics Subject Classification, and further useful tools. AMS journal article templates are available from Overleaf; language editing services are available from Charlesworth Author Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and electronic access for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints are provided free of charge in electronic form to all authors. A downloadable and printable PDF version of each article is available from the AMS website following print publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification email containing access information is sent to all authors as soon as an issue is published in print; this electronic delivery provides authors with permanent electronic access to their published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions and reuse policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual readers of this publication, and nonprofit libraries acting for them, are permitted to make fair use of the material, such as to copy an article for use in teaching or research. Permission is granted to quote brief passages from this publication in reviews, provided the customary acknowledgment of the source is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republication, systematic copying, or multiple reproduction of any material is permitted only under license from the AMS; requests are handled by the Copyright Clearance Center. Material for which the author holds copyright is excluded from AMS license provisions; permission requests for such material should be addressed directly to the author(s). Copyright ownership is indicated in the notice in the lower right-hand corner of the first page of each article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and subscription policy / free digital archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Full article PDFs in all volumes older than five years are available electronically free of charge. A current active subscription to the electronic version of this journal is required to view article PDFs in all volumes published within the last five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription information and links are provided on the site; free archive covers older than five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal is indexed in Mathematical Reviews®, Zentralblatt MATH, Science Citation Index®, Science Citation Index—Expanded, ISI Alerting Services, CompuMath Citation Index®, and Current Contents®, Physical, Chemical & Earth Sciences. This journal is archived in Portico and in CLOCKSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing and archiving services used by the journal are listed for author/institutional awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance inquiries and prepress contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inquiries concerning a paper that has been accepted for publication that cannot be answered via the manuscript tracking system should be sent by email or by postal mail to the Electronic PrePress Department, American Mathematical Society, 201 Charles Street, Providence, RI 02904-2213 USA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details provided for handling post-acceptance administrative or production questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of accessible mathematics content
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content are available as a resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult these guidelines when preparing graphics and other materials to ensure accessibility; 'Preparing graphics' and related tools are listed under Useful Tools.
